title: What is known about 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine acts on a list of blocks of 1s: Lean proves every rule by which the head meets a block or a separator, and that it halts exactly on F> 0 0 1. A leftward pass computes a running parity, and the run is organised in epochs that grow the tape by a factor about 1.75. In 1010 steps F met two 0s in a row only at the right end of the tape, with blank tape beyond (observed). Whether that always holds is not settled.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The leftward sweep is a running parity
claims.text: With the head in D (even) or C (odd) on the last cell of a 4-cell word 111x: D on u = 1110 leaves 0101 and goes to C; D on v = 1111 leaves 1111 and stays D; C on u leaves 1111 and goes to D; C on v leaves 0101 and stays C. So the word written behind the head is the running XOR (from the right) of the u's, as 1111 (even) or 0101 (odd). Plus the runs (1111)n for D, E and F.

claims.title: The machine on blocks of 1s
claims.text: Going right, F crosses a block; at a separator followed by a block of one cell it fills the separator, erases the cell and fills the next separator (the blocks on both sides gain a cell); at a separator followed by a longer block it turns, moving two cells from that block to the one on its left; three 0s before a 1 are filled; at four 0s it writes 1011 and turns. Going left, D crosses a block and fills the separator after it; E erases every second cell of the next block and, if the block's length is odd, the pass goes on in D, otherwise the head turns. Each statement holds for any tape around the pattern.

claims.title: Every turn of F is at a block of odd length, except at the right end (10<sup>10</sup> steps)
claims.text: In the first 1010 steps F turned 139,833 times. The block it turned at had odd length every time (3 cells 36,463 times, 5 cells 46,436, 7 cells 19,254, 9 cells 20,280, and longer), except 22 turns at a block of exactly two cells, each of which was the last block of the tape. A turn at a block of two with another block after it would leave 0 0 1 (turn_two). F met two 0s in a row 42 times, each time at the right end with only blank cells beyond. No halt.

claims.title: Two phases in an epoch
claims.text: Followed turn by turn through one epoch (steps 4,104 to 7,890): first the head bounces between the left end and a turning place that moves right, eating the blocks beyond it two cells at a time; at each right turn the zone is a list of blocks 14k+3, at each left turn blocks 14k+1 separated by odd numbers of one-cell blocks. When the turning place reaches the right end the head crosses back to the left end in short bounces, leaving blocks of 3 and pairs 1, 5 (the words 1110 and 1011) for the next epoch to eat. Observed on that epoch, not proved.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only B reading 1 halts; B is entered only from A reading 0, and A only from F reading 0. So the machine halts exactly on F> 0 0 1: F on that pattern halts within two steps (halt_F), and two steps before any halt the machine is in F on 0 0 1 (halt_route). An earlier version of this page gave the pattern as F> 1 0 1, which was wrong.

claims.title: Epochs to 3·10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: Sweeps across 80% of the tape begin epochs at steps 2,284, 5,873, 13,248, 47,799, 145,962, 487,979, 1,427,948, 4,277,179, 13,419,889, 40,483,837, 124,076,294, 383,276,545 and 1,162,585,978, with the left end at 56, 103, 172, 374, 703, 1,319, 2,265, 4,020, 7,237, 12,641, 22,085, 38,918 and 68,091 cells; the right end grows by about 10 cells per epoch (130 at the end). Ratio per epoch: about 1.75 in length, 3 in time.
claims.where: c/epochs.c (copy of the tool in the first machine of this batch)

claims.title: A twin machine
claims.text: The holdout 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF has exactly this machine's configuration (tape, head position, state) at 12 of the 13 epoch starts up to 1.7·109 steps, reaching each about 1.5 times later.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with K = 3, 4, 5, 6 leaves abstract halting configurations; the n-gram CPS decider (widths 3 to 7, with history and LRU) fails; no conserved quantity a·ones + b·pos + W[state] mod 2..12 (bbtools.invariants).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 64,917 cells have been visited and 53,447 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.064).

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 12 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs F> 0 0 1. In the run so far two 0s in a row appear in front of F only at the right end of the tape, with blank tape beyond. A proof would need an invariant that keeps every block at which F turns odd, and a description of what the right end does once per epoch.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF goes through 4,995,966 configurations of 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF in its first 10<sup>7</sup> steps, in order, about 1.5 times slower. The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 64,917 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A word in two 4-cell letters
html:
Between sweeps the tape is a long run of blocks 14k+30, that is a word in two letters, u = 1110 and v = 1111. At step 2,003,981 the tape begins

u^3 v u v^2 u v u v u^3 v^2 u v u v u v^2 u^2 v^3 u v^2 u v^3 u v u^3 ...

about 650 letters in all, plus a short end on the right. Read u as 1 and v as 0: the tape holds a binary string about 650 bits long (the side that grows like a square root), next to a short fixed part on the right (the side that grows like a logarithm).

sections.heading: Every leftward sweep computes a running parity
html: Going left, the head is in state D ("even so far") or C ("odd so far"). Each time it crosses a letter: if the letter is u the parity flips. It writes 1111 behind it when the new parity is even and 0101 when it is odd. These four cases (and the long runs over 1111) are proved in Lean.

Worked example: the word v u u v u (bits 0 1 1 0 1) swept from the right, starting even: u → odd, v → odd, u → even, u → odd, v → odd: the new bits, left to right, are 1 1 0 1 1. The next rightward sweep turns 0101 back into a letter; repeating "replace by running XOR" is the rule that generates Pascal's triangle modulo 2, which is why the space-time diagram is full of Sierpinski triangles.

sections.heading: Epochs, each about 1.75 times longer
html: The head does not always cross the whole tape. Inside an epoch it bounces between the left end and an inner wall; the wall moves left a little on each bounce, and the zone between them is rewritten by the parity rule while the tape right of the wall stays frozen. When the zone has shrunk away, a full crossing starts a new epoch. Epochs began at steps 47,799, 145,962, 487,979, 1,427,948, 4,277,179, 13,419,889, 40,483,837, 124,076,294, 383,276,545 and 1,162,585,978, with the tape's left end at 374, 703, 1,319, 2,265, 4,020, 7,237, 12,641, 22,085, 38,918 and 68,091 cells.

Followed turn by turn, an epoch has two phases (observed on the epoch from step 4,104 to 7,890). In the first the head bounces between the left end and a turning place that moves right by 2 to 20 cells per bounce, eating the blocks beyond it two cells at a time. When the turning place reaches the right end of the tape, the head crosses back to the left end in short bounces 8 to 28 cells wide, leaving blocks of 3 and pairs 1, 5 behind it, which the next epoch eats.

sections.heading: Only on F> 0 0 1
html: The machine stops only when B reads a 1; B is entered only from A reading 0, and A only from F reading 0. So it stops exactly when state F stands on 0 0 1 (proved in Lean, both directions). An earlier version of this page said 1 0 1, which was wrong.

Read the tape as blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. Going right, F crosses blocks; a block of one cell is erased and its two separators filled; at a longer block F turns, moving two cells from that block to the block on its left. A turn at a block of exactly two cells erases it, and if another block follows, the tape now reads 0 0 1 there: the next visit of F would stop the machine. All of these rules are Lean theorems.

In the first 1010 steps F turned 139,833 times, always at a block of odd length, except 22 times at a block of two that was the last block on the tape, with nothing but blank cells after it. F met two 0s in a row 42 times, always at that right end. So far, then, the question is decided at the right end of the tape, about twice per epoch. This is what the run shows, not a proof: nothing yet shows that a block of even length can never be turned at in the middle of the tape.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.064).
After 109 steps the tape spans 64,917 cells (43,020 left of the start, 130 right), with a density of 1s of 0.823.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF is a slowed-down copy of this machine (observed, not proved). Read that machine's states A as A, B as B, D as C, E as E, F as F of this machine. Then 4,995,966 of its first 107 configurations (tape, head position and state) are configurations of this machine, in the same order. The last one is step 9,999,982 there and step 6,664,008 here, so it takes about 1.5 times as many steps. The tables are not renamings of each other. Lean proves (lean/Twin.lean in the other machine's folder, sim_or_break, not_halts_of_noBreak) that each step of the faster machine is matched by one or three steps of the slower one up to the first break, a configuration where the paired states act differently, and that neither machine halts if no break ever comes. A halt of either machine is itself a break, and the halting transitions of the two do not correspond, so the two are not known to halt together.

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→A, E→B, F→C and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B; it is this table started in state E
  • 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A binary word written in 4-cell letters 1110 and 1111; every leftward sweep replaces it by its running parity (XOR from the right), so the space-time diagram is Pascal's triangle mod 2 (Sierpinski triangles), in epochs that each grow the tape by about 1.75.
